title: 16S Metagenomics Bioinformatics Workflow — Pre/Post Test
notes: No participant code; pairing uses the signed-in dashboard account.
Only knowledge-check MCQs are auto-scored (I don't know yet = 0).
Background, confidence, and reflection items are stored but not scored.

pre_test.question: Which best describes your current role?
Before this training, how much exposure had you had to 16S metagenomics?
options: None—I am new to the topic
I have read about it or attended a lecture

pre_test.question: How many 16S datasets have you analyzed before this training?
Which tools have you used before? Select all that apply.
Which skill would you most like to develop during this training? Select one.
options: Processing reads with QIIME 2 and DADA2
Analyzing alpha and beta diversity in R

pre_test.question: I can navigate files and run basic commands in Linux/Bash.
pre_test.sectionIntro: Rate your confidence before training using this scale: 1 = Not at all confident; 2 = Slightly confident; 3 = Moderately confident; 4 = Very confident; 5 = Extremely confident

pre_test.question: I can explain why the 16S rRNA gene is used to profile microbial communities.
I can describe and carry out the main QIIME 2 workflow from reads to taxonomy.
I can analyze and interpret alpha and beta diversity using R/phyloseq.
I can explain what PICRUSt2 predicts and recognize the limits of those predictions.
Why is the 16S rRNA gene useful for profiling bacteria and archaea?
options: It is found only in organisms that can be cultured
It combines conserved regions with variable regions that help distinguish taxa
It directly measures all genes and pathways in a community
It changes completely from one cell to another
pre_test.sectionIntro: Choose the one best answer. Select "I don't know yet" instead of guessing if you are unsure.

pre_test.question: Which conclusion is most directly supported by a typical 16S rRNA amplicon dataset?
options: The relative taxonomic composition of the sampled microbial community
The exact absolute number of every organism in the environment
The complete genome of every organism in the sample
The measured activity of every metabolic pathway

pre_test.question: What information does a FASTQ file contain?
options: Taxonomic names and abundance percentages only
Sequence reads and their associated quality scores

pre_test.question: Which Linux command displays the current working directory?
Which sequence shows the most appropriate order for the main processing steps?
options: FastQC → adapter/primer trimming → DADA2 denoising → taxonomic classification
DADA2 denoising → demultiplexing → FastQC → taxonomic classification

pre_test.question: What is the main purpose of a manifest file when importing sequences into QIIME 2?
options: To connect sample IDs to the locations of their sequence files
To store the taxonomic classification of each ASV

pre_test.question: Which pair is a key output of DADA2 denoising in the module's QIIME 2 workflow?
options: A metadata file and a bar plot
An ASV count table and representative sequences
A raw FASTQ file and a reference database
A pathway table and a PCoA plot

pre_test.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes alpha diversity from beta diversity?
options: Alpha diversity compares communities; beta diversity describes one community
Alpha diversity describes diversity within a sample; beta diversity compares composition among samples
Alpha diversity uses only taxonomy; beta diversity uses only phylogeny
They are two names for the same measurement

pre_test.question: What does a plateau in a sample's alpha-rarefaction curve generally suggest?
options: Sequencing depth likely captured most of the detectable taxa in that sample
All samples have identical community composition
Taxonomic classification was performed at 100% confidence

pre_test.question: What does PICRUSt2 provide in this workflow?
options: Predictions of gene-family and pathway abundances from marker-gene data
Removal of primers from raw reads
Assignment of reads to samples using barcodes

pre_test.question: In one sentence, what is your biggest question about analyzing 16S data?
